decisions.location: Background, p. 195 (lines 88-93); Measures, p. 196 (lines 172-175); References, p. 200 (lines 830-834)
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly names Zigler and Balla (1972) as one of the original studies it conceptually replicates, constructing the Dice-Hole Task (DHT) based on Zigler and Balla's (1972) 'Marble in the Hole' task to test positive- and negative-reaction tendencies (responsiveness to social reinforcement) between participants with intellectual disability and controls. Both the shipped row and blind target 2 accurately identify this tested original work.

decisions.reason: In both the specific generalized linear mixed-effects analysis of the Dice-Hole Task (which adapted Zigler & Balla, 1972, finding no group effect on the first trial or on the difference between trials after multiple-comparison adjustment) and the explicit overall replication verdict in the Discussion, the authors conclude that their results do not support the hypothesized differences between people with intellectual disability and control groups and are not in accordance with the previous studies by Zigler and colleagues. Under the codebook hierarchy, this explicit negative overall verdict and specific task result establish the outcome as 'failed'.

decisions.location: Abstract, p. 194 (lines 24-29); Participants and procedure, p. 196 (lines 144-183)
decisions.reason: The authors collected new experimental data from a fresh sample of 75 Polish students (25 special vocational school students with mild intellectual disability, 25 mainstream vocational school controls, and 25 primary school controls) using newly prepared experimental tasks to conceptually re-test the published findings of Zigler and Balla (1972) and colleagues. Re-testing a published finding with newly collected data in a different sample is a 'replication'.
